games.title: Cactus or Fern?
games.skillName: How plants' needs vary from plant to plant
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore the requirements of plants for life and growth (air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow) and how they vary from plant to plant
games.instruction: Compare the plants, then tap the best answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about where this plant grows in the wild, then try again.

questions.ask: Which plant needs the least water?
Which plant grows best in a damp, shady wood?
Which plant grows with its roots under water in a pond?
Which plant needs lots of bright sunshine to grow tall?
A cactus has a thick, fleshy stem. What is it for?
Which plant can grow on a bare rock or wall with almost no soil?
A Venus flytrap grows in poor, boggy soil. Why does it catch insects?
Where would a fern grow best?
Which plant needs the most room to grow?
Which plant has spines instead of wide leaves to save water?

games.title: Sun Safe Eyes
games.skillName: Protecting your eyes from the Sun
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous and that there are ways to protect their eyes
games.instruction: Read each sentence, then tap true or false.
games.hint: Not quite. Remember the Sun's light is strong enough to hurt your eyes, then try again.

questions.ask: You should never look straight at the Sun.
Looking at the Sun through binoculars is safe.
Sunglasses help protect your eyes from bright sunlight.
Any dark sunglasses are safe for staring at the Sun.
A sun hat with a wide brim can help shade your eyes.
Sunlight can still harm your eyes on a cloudy day.
It is safe to look at the Sun if you only do it for a minute.
Good sunglasses block harmful UV light.
Sunlight reflecting off snow or water can hurt your eyes.
Looking at the Sun through a telescope is safe if you squint.
